findings_to_judge.finding: Sunbelt's buyback has been throttled by roughly 85%: treasury shares rose only from 3,993,501 (29 May 2026) to 4,699,397 (28 Aug 2026) — 705,896 shares in 13 weeks, ~54k/week or ~$4m/week at prevailing prices, an annualised ~$210m — versus $1,413m of buybacks in FY26 and 405,000 shares in the single week of 6-10 April 2026 under the same $1.5bn programme launched 2 March 2026; shares outstanding are flat at ~409.8m and the weekly notices show the pace decaying monotonically (405k Apr 6-10, 135k Apr 13-17, 75k Apr 27-May 1, 60k May 26-29, 60k Jun 15-18, 43k Jul 6-10, 17k Aug 10-14, 13k Aug 17-21, 23k Aug 24-28, 47k Aug 31-Sep 4).

The Q1 FY27 (May-July 2026) volume setup is unusually well supported and the margin worry is pre-guided: the comp is +2.4% group rental revenue in Q1 FY26, Q4 FY26 exited at +8.0%, the $650m Reliant/Aries modular business closed 1 May 2026 so the full quarter is inorganically boosted, management flagged ~$70m of Q1-specific FIFA World Cup and UFC event revenue on the June call and said margins improve 'in the back half', and both peers reported record calendar Q2 and RAISED full-year guidance (URI rental revenue +12.7%, fleet productivity +3.4%, FY revenue guide lifted to $17.5-17.8bn from $16.9-17.4bn on 22 July; Herc rental revenue +23%, guidance raised on 28 July).
